A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Guiding Token-Sparse Diffusion Models. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, sparsity analyses, and evaluations of its trained TR-DIT-2.5B model using GenEval and HPSv3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds guidance-baseline results, an interaction-strategy comparison and qualitative sparsity sweeps.

M1.justification: Appendix D adds alternative CFG–SG inference combinations with separate guidance weights and different prediction branches, including Inner, Compositional and IP2P-style rules. The core SG equations, model architectures and training objectives remain unchanged; combining SG with AutoGuidance was already documented in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ImageNet-256, training on recaptioned COYO data supplemented by JourneyDB and FLUX-6M, and GenEval/HPSv3 evaluation. The added comparisons and prompt-specific sweeps remain within the existing image-generation tasks and domains.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds evaluated APG and S2 baselines alongside the retained CFG, AutoGuidance and ICG comparisons. Appendix D also compares alternative guidance-interaction rules. The ImageNet state-of-the-art and text-to-image comparator sets otherwise remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The displayed routing sweep changes from guidance scales 1.4 and 1.6 in v1 Figure 8 to 1.1, 1.5 and 1.9 in v2 Figure 6. New interaction experiments compare FID and function evaluations per step. Existing training budgets, samplers and 50k/5k FID protocols remain unchanged; these reporting changes do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests which of four CFG–SG interaction rules works best. Figures A4–A5 add qualitative sparsity sweeps for chameleon and pottery prompts, while the main sensitivity plots are revised. These focused additions supplement the existing routing/masking, checkpoint and diversity analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added numerical comparisons retain single-value reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 newly reports APG FID 2.51 and S2 FID 3.12. Table A3 adds interaction FIDs of 2.14, 10.70, 11.14 and 2.62. Revised plots and new qualitative grids add further results, while headline ImageNet FID 1.58, HPSv3 9.87 and GenEval 0.62 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix D introduces explicit mathematical definitions for four guidance compositions in Equations A5–A8. The existing flow-matching definitions and auxiliary MAE derivation in Equations A1–A4 are unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: finetuning-free sparse guidance, improved quality and inference efficiency, and applicability to a 2.5B text-to-image model. The headline quantitative claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning capacity gaps, diversity preservation, routing versus masking and AutoGuidance checkpoint flexibility are retained. The added interaction ranking reports outcomes without introducing a substantive new causal interpretation, applicability boundary or limitation.

D1.justification: Figures A4–A5 supply full prompts and displayed sparsity settings for the new qualitative sweeps. Existing architecture and optimizer tables, checkpoint schedules, benchmark settings and project access information are retained. Appendix D does not specify the guidance weights used for its comparison.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting APG and stochastic self-guidance, changes the cited sources for sFID and the Llama architecture, and retains the broader research positioning. Numerous publication-metadata updates and consolidation of duplicate SiT references do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording, capitalization, caption and cross-reference edits, and explicitly identifies the AutoGuidance combination behind SGFID in the main text. It adds a supplementary-material heading and an interaction section, moving Qualitative Samples from Appendix D to E; the main narrative remains largely intact.

P2.justification: Figures 6 and 8 exchange analytical roles and receive revised panels, labels and color scales. Table 2 gains rows, and Table A3 plus Figures A4–A5 are added. Appendix tables are resized and repositioned; existing sample galleries are retained under updated numbering.

improvement.justification: The added baseline comparisons and qualitative sparsity sweeps modestly strengthen empirical support, while clearer main-text attribution explains the retained SGFID result. Reporting issues limit the gain: Section 4.2 still calls CFG the next-best comparator despite APG's better score, and Appendix D reports two evaluations for a Direct formula containing three prediction branches without explaining a weight choice that removes one. These localized issues constrain the new analysis but leave the established evidence intact.
